title: Smt. Rekha Satija vs Deepika on 19 July, 2016
full_text: Smt. Rekha Satija vs Deepika on 19 July, 2016 IN THE COURT OF MS. SHUCHI LALER, SCJ CUM RC (SHAHDARA) KKD COURTS, DELHI. RC / ARC No. 108/2016 Smt. Rekha Satija W/o Sh. Sachin Satija R/o F-2, Radheypuri, School Lane, Delhi 110051 ....Petitioner Versus Deepika Ground floor, C-1/9, Krishna Nagar, Delhi 110051 ....Respondent Date of institution of petition : 08.06.2011 Final arguments heard on : 30.05.2016 Judgment announced on : 19.07.2016 APPLICATION FOR EVICTION OF TENANT UNDER SECTION 14 (1) (a) OF DELHI RENT CONTROL ACT, 1958 (HEREINAFTER REFERRED TO AS 'DRC ACT') JUDGMENT : 1. Eviction in respect of a shop situated at ground floor of the property bearing No. C-1/9, Krishna Nagar, Lal Quarter, Delhi - 110 051 (henceforth referred to as tenanted shop) has been sought on the ground that the respondent / tenant had defaulted in payment of rent despite service of demand notice, hence, committed 'first default', as envisaged under Clause (a) to the proviso of sub-section (1) of Section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 1 of 25 Act, 1958 (in short ' DRC Act '). PETITION 2. Brief narration of the facts as disclosed in the petition is as under: 2.1 That petitioner is the landlady and owner of the tenanted shop by virtue of relinquishment deed dated 20.04.2009 executed by the erstwhile landlord Mr. Subhash Tandon in her favour. 2.2 That the tenanted shop was let out to the respondent by Mr. Subhash Tandon and the monthly rent is Rs.900/- besides other charges. 2.3 That a letter of attornment dated 22.04.2009 was sent to the respondent thereby informing her about the change in ownership of the tenanted shop. 2.4 That the respondent failed to pay or tender the monthly rent despite service of legal demand notice dated 11.05.2009. Being aggrieved, the petitioner filed the present petition. WRITTEN STATEMENT 3. Written statement has been filed on behalf of the respondent wherein she has taken preliminary objections such as the present eviction petition has not been instituted in correct name of respondent; the present petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties; petitioner has no locus standi to file the RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 2 of 25 present petition; the petition does not reveal any cause of action and eviction petition under Section 14 (1) (a) is not maintainable. The averments to the contrary made by the respondent are as under :- 3.1 That the eviction petition describes the tenant as 'Deepika' whereas the actual tenant of the tenanted shop is 'Deepika Gupta'. 3.2 That Sh. Subhash Tandon had executed a Registered Power of Attorney in favour of Smt. Amrita Tandon and had given her the right to collect rent. 3.3 That the respondent has been regularly paying rent to Sh. Subhash Tandon and thereafter to Ms. Amrita Tandon till date and thereafter, she has deposited rent before the court for the period from December, 2009 onwards. The rate of rent is Rs. 430/- pm excluding water and electricity charges. 3.4 That Sh. Subhash Tandon could not have transferred 50% share of Smt. Amrita Tandon in favour of petitioner by way of Relinquishment Deed. 3.5 That the respondent has deposited the rent for the period from December, 2009 to June, 2011 under Section 27 DRC Act by way of D.R. Petition No. 119/2010 and D.R. Petition No. 267/11. 3.6 That no proper demand notice as required under law has been served upon the respondent. The demand notice, if any, placed on record is defective and does not meet the requirements of law. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 3 of 25 In view thereof, the respondent has alleged that the petitioner is not entitled for any relief and prayed for dismissal of the present petition with cost. PETITIONER'S EVIDENCE 4. In support of her case, the petitioner stepped into the witness box as PW 1. She has tendered her evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/X. PW 1 has relied upon the following documents:- ➢ Site Plan as Mark A; ➢ Relinquishment Deed as Ex. PW1/C; ➢ Legal Notice and Postal Receipt as Ex. PW1/H and Ex. PW1/I. The aforesaid witness was duly cross-examined by ld. counsel for respondent. Thereafter, the petitioner closed her evidence. RESPONDENT'S EVIDENCE 5. In rebuttal, the respondent stepped into the witness box as RW-1 and she has tendered her evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex. R-1. Respondent has relied upon the following documents:- ➢ Rent Receipts as Ex. RW1/1 (colly); RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 4 of 25 ➢ Copy of Challans and orders as Ex. RW1/2; ➢ Copy of Will as Mark A. ➢ Copy of GPA as Mark B. The aforesaid witness was duly cross-examined by ld. counsel for petitioner. Thereafter, the respondent closed her evidence. FINAL ARGUMENTS 6. Rival submissions advanced at bar have been heard and record perused with the assistance of Ld. Counsels for parties. JUDICIAL RESOLUTION 7. In order to be entitled to an eviction order under clause (a) of sub section 1 of Section 14 of DRC Act, the petitioner is required to prove : 1. Relationship of landlord and tenant; 2. Existence of arrears of rent legally recoverable as on date of service of demand notice; 3. Service of notice of demand; 4. Failure of the tenant to pay / tender the entire legally recoverable arrears of rent within stipulated period of two months from the date of service of demand notice. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 5 of 25 RELATIONSHIP OF LANDLORD AND TENANT 8. The respondent has refuted the jural relationship of landlord - tenant between the parties and has claimed that Ms. Amrita Tandon is her landlady. It is an admitted case of the parties that the property in question was initially owned by Sh. Satender Singh who had executed a Sale Deed in favour of parents of petitioner Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon and Smt. Darshana Rani. 9. The respondent has claimed that Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon had solemnized marriage with Smt. Amrita Tandon after his first wife Ms. Darshana Rani expired and had executed registered Will and registered GPA dated 28.09.2007, Mark A and Mark B, in her favour and thereafter, the respondent is regularly paying rent to her landlady Ms. Amrita Tandon. 10. The petitioner, per contra, averred that Smt. Amrita Tandon was hired as a care taker during illness of her father Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon and she is not legally wedded wife of Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon. The petitioner claimed herself to be the owner and landlord of the tenanted shop by virtue of registered relinquishment deed dated 20.04.2009 Ex.PW1/C. 11. It is pertinent to mention that during the pendency of the instant eviction petition, Ms. Amrita Tandon had filed an application under Order I Rule 10 CPC for her impleadment as petitioner no. 2. The said application was dismissed by Ld. Predecessor vide Order dated 21.05.2012. 12. In this background, the court would examine the RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 6 of 25 validity and legality of documents such as registered Will and registered GPA dated 28.09.2007, Mark A and Mark B respectively executed by father of petitioner in favour of Ms. Amrita Tandon, consequently, its impact upon the status of petitioner as landlady. 13. The respondent has placed reliance upon a copy of GPA dated 28.09.2007 Mark B by virtue of which Ms. Amrita Tandon has been authorized to collect rent on behalf of Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon and also to manage the affairs pertaining to property in question. By execution of GPA dated 28.09.2007 Mark B, Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon did not transfer any right, title or interest with respect to the property in question in favour of Ms. Amrita Tandon. 14. In the case titled as Suraj Lamps & Industries Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Haryana & Anr. AIR 2012 SC 206 the Hon'ble Supreme Court, while discussing the scope of Power of Attorney, has observed in para no. 13 as under: "13. A power of attorney is not an instrument of transfer in regard to any right, title or interest in an immovable property. The power of attorney is creation of an agency whereby the grantor authorizes the grantee to do the acts specified therein, on behalf of grantor, which when executed will be binding on the grantor as if done by him (see Section 1A and Section 2 of Powers of Attorney Act, 1882). It is revocable or terminable at any time unless it is made irrevocable in a manner known to law. Even an irrevocable attorney does not have the effect of transferring title to the grantee......" 15. Thus, it is apparent that by execution of GPA Mark B, RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 7 of 25 Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon did not convey title in favour of Ms. Amrita Tandon. Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon did not divest himself of his rights in the property in question and Ms. Amrita Tandon was merely an attorney / agent of Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon who was authorized to do certain acts specified in the GPA Mark B. 16. A Power of Attorney can be revoked or terminated as enumerated under Section 201 to 203 of Contract Act. The GPA Mark B does not record or recognize an interest of Smt. Amrita Tandon in the property in question so as to make it irrevocable under Section 202 of Contract Act. The said GPA merely authorizes Ms. Amrita Tandon as an agent to do certain acts in the name or on behalf of the executant / Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon. Thus, GPA Mark B was revocable and terminable. Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon by execution of registered relinquishment deed dated 20.04.2009 Ex.PW1/C in favour of the petitioner impliedly revoked GPA Mark B in terms of Section 207 of Contract Act. 17. Now, adverting to the second document i.e. the registered Will dated 28.09.2007 Mark A executed by father of petitioner Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon in favour of Smt. Amrita Tandon. A 'Will' is a posthumous disposition of the estate of the testator directing distribution of his estate upon his death. The two essential characteristics of a Will are that it is intended to come into effect only after the death of the testator and is revocable at any time during the life time of the testator. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 8 of 25 Registration of a Will does not make it any more effective. 18. In the instant case, Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon, during his life time, executed registered relinquishment deed Ex.PW1/C whereby he transferred his right and title in the property in question in favour of petitioner. The execution of registered relinquishment deed Ex.PW1/C operates as revocation of Will Mark A. 19. In view of above, the court is of the opinion that the documents such as Will and GPA dated 28.09.2007 Mark A and B did not confer any title or right upon Ms. Amrita Tandon qua the property in question. Ms. Amrita Tandon was merely an agent who was authorized by way of GPA Mark B to collect rent from the respondent on behalf of Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon. The petitioner, by virtue of registered relinquishment deed Ex.PW1/C and being the daughter of Ms. Darshana Tandon and Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon, is a co-owner / landlady qua the tenanted shop. RATE OF RENT 20. Now coming to the contentious issue regarding rate of rent. The petitioner has averred that the tenanted shop was let out to the respondent @ Rs. 900/- pm besides other facility whereas the respondent has claimed the rate of rent to be Rs. 430/- pm excluding water and electricity charges. 21. No Rent Agreement has been filed on record to show RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 9 of 25 as to what was the agreed rent. The petitioner / PW1, in her cross-examination, stated that she cannot tell the actual rate of rent of the respondent as it is already mentioned in the said letter. PW1 admitted that she has not mentioned the rate of rent in the demand notice Ex.PW1/H. PW1 also testified that she does not have any document except the hand written letter of her father in respect of description of tenants in the property. No such letter has been filed on record in the instant eviction petition. Thus, there is no document in support of petitioner's version regarding rate of rent being Rs. 900/- pm. On the contrary, the respondent has filed on record the rent receipts of the period 01.12.2008 to 31.12.2008, 01.07.2001 to 31.07.2001 and 01.11.2009 to 30.11.2009 Ex.RW1/2 (colly) wherein the rate of rent is mentioned as Rs. 430/- pm. Nothing substantial has been extracted during cross-examination of RW1 with respect to the rent receipts Ex. RW1/1 so as to cast a doubt on its genuineness. 22. There is no document such as counter foil of previous rent receipts, books of accounts, ITRs or Bank Statement etc. to show that the agreed rate of rent was Rs. 900/- per month. That being the situation upon preponderance of probabilities, the rate of rent cannot be fixed at the rate of Rs. 900/- per month. The version of respondent regarding rate of rent being Rs. 430/- per month is to be accepted. SERVICE OF VALID DEMAND NOTICE 23. The service of a valid notice of demand furnishes the RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 10 of 25 cause of action for an eviction petition under Section 14 (1) (a) DRC Act. A valid demand notice is a pre cursor to filing of eviction petition on the ground of non payment of rent. In the instant case, the demand notice Ex.PW1/H has been issued on 11.05.2009, demanding rent for the month of April 2009. 24. The core question which arises for consideration is : Whether the demand notice Ex.PW1/H issued prior to 15 th of next month would be a valid legal notice for the purpose of section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act in view of section 26 of the Act? 25. Section 26(1) of Delhi Rent Control Act reads as under:- "26. Receipt to be given for rent paid. - (1) Every tenant shall pay rent within the time fixed by contract or in the absence of such contract, by the fifteenth day of the month next following the month for which it is payable and where any default occurs in the payment of rent, the tenant shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of fifteen per cent. per annum from the date on which such payment of rent is due to the date on which it is paid." (emphasis supplied) 26. In the present case, there is no contract for advance payment of rent / periodical payment. Hence, the statutory provision i.e. Section 26 (1) DRC Act comes into play. The tenant / respondent was required to pay the rent to the landlady by 15th day of the month next following the month for which it was payable. Accordingly, the rent for the month of April, 2009 becomes due / the respondent can make valid tender of the rent RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 11 of 25 till 15th day of May i.e. 15 days in the next succeeding month and as such on 11.05.2009 (i.e. the date of demand notice Ex.PW1/H), the rent was yet not due as the due date was 15.05.2009. 27. Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act provides as under:- "(a) that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of the rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served of him by the landlord in the manner provided in section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (4 of 1882);" (emphasis supplied) 28. The essential requirements of section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act have been culled out in judgment titled Daulat Ram vs Som Nath AIR 1981 Del 354 in the paragraph reproduced below:- "The cause of action for eviction on the ground of non- payment of rent thus consists of the following facts : i) Relationship of landlord and tenant; ii) Existence of arrears of rent legally recoverable on the date of notice of demand; iii) Service of notice of demand in the manner provided in Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act; and iv) Failure of the tenant to pay or tender the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date of service of notice." (emphasis supplied) 29. One of the essential requirement for invoking the provision of Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act, is that on RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 12 of 25 the date of notice, the tenant should be in arrears of rent. The words used in section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act are "notice of demand for the arrears of rent". Therefore, the notice of demand should be of the arrears of rent and not of the rent which is not due and would become due on a date subsequent to the date of notice. As per Black's Law Dictionary, Second Edition 'arrears' means "A remaining debt or liability after the due date." 30. In the present case, the due date for the payment of rent of the month of April 2009, was 15.05.2009, but the notice has been issued on 11.05.2009. On 11.05.2009 the due date for the payment of rent of the month of April 2009, had yet not arrived and as such the tenant was not in arrears of rent for the month of April on 11.05.2009. The tenant could have been in the arrears of rent for the month of April 2009 only after 15.05.2009 and not prior thereto. Therefore, the notice dated 11.05.2009 issued by the petitioner to the respondent is an invalid notice as it demands rent for the month of April 2009, of which the respondent was not in arrears as on 11.05.2009. 31. The same conclusion can also be reached by a different reasoning as well. Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act provides as under:- "(a) that the tenant has neither paid nor tendered the whole of the arrears of the rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date on which a notice of demand for the arrears of rent has been served of him by the landlord in the manner provided in section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (4 of 1882);" (emphasis supplied) RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 13 of 25 32. Another pre requisite of Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act, is that the rent which is demanded in the notice should be legally recoverable from the tenant. The term 'legally recoverable', in simple words mean, something that can be recovered by filing a suit. Therefore, the question before the court is: Whether the petitioner in the present case could have legally recovered the rent of April 2009 from the respondent / tenant on 11.05.2009? 33. To answer the said question, the court needs to ascertain as to what would be the fate of a suit for recovery of rent of April 2009, if it was filed on 11.05.2009. If the suit was filed by the petitioner in order to recover the rent of April 2009 from the respondent on 11.05.2009, the said suit would have been rejected1 being premature and being without any cause of action, as the rent was yet not due. Hence, the rent for the said period 2 would not have been legally recoverable on 11.05.2009. Therefore, even on this ground, the legal notice dated 11.05.2009 is defective and cannot form the basis of an eviction petition. 34. There is another aspect which needs to be taken into consideration i.e. Whether sending of the legal notice dated 11.05.2009 on 19.05.2009 and its receiving by the respondent after due date i.e. 15.05.2009 would make the demand notice Ex.PW1/H valid? 35. In the present case, the legal notice is dated 1 Order VII Rule 11(a) 2 April 2009. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 14 of 25 11.05.2009 but it has been posted on 19.05.2009, therefore, it has been received by the respondent after 15.05.2009, i.e. after the expiry of the due date for making the payment of rent of April 2009. The court is of the opinion that the posting of notice dated 11.05.2009 on 19.05.2009 would not make it a valid demand notice for the following manifold reasons:- A. Because, the demand would be adjudged from the date mentioned in the legal notice Ex.PW1/H. When a date is mentioned in the legal notice Ex.PW1/H, it means that on said date, the landlord is raising demand / asking the tenant to pay arrears of rent. In the present case, the demand has been made on 11.05.2009 and not on 19.05.2009, as the legal notice has been signed on 11.05.2009. The court is required to see as to whether on 11.05.2009, the demand raised in notice was legal or not. The date of posting of notice or of its service is irrelevant. B. Because, a tenant would comply with the terms of a demand notice considering the date mentioned therein and would not search for a date of its posting or service. A recipient of notice can easily find out the date of the notice, as the same is mentioned in the notice itself, however, it is difficult to search for the date on which the notice was posted. A recipient of legal notice is expected to act upon the notice as it is and cannot be expected to find out the date of posting of the legal notice in order to act upon the same. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 15 of 25 Therefore, a legal notice which is premature on the date when it was signed, even if it was posted after the requisite date, the said action of the sender of posting the legal notice subsequently would not render the demand notice legal and valid. If the sender is intelligent enough to post the legal notice after the cause of action to raise the demand actually accrued, then he should have corrected the date on the legal notice, before posting it and he should not have left it for the recipient to find out as to whether the legal notice which is premature, as per the date mentioned on the notice, was posted after the cause of action to issue the notice matured. In the present case, the legal notice was signed on 11.05.2009, but was posted on 19.05.2009. However, the respondent was neither required, nor had the means, to find out as to whether the legal notice was posted on 11.05.2009 or whether it was posted after 15.05.2009 i.e. on 19.05.2009. The respondent was required to act upon the legal notice Ex.PW1/H as per the date mentioned therein i.e. 11.05.2009 and on the said date, no rent was due upon him. C. Because, the demand notice Ex.PW1/H has been issued by the petitioner in anticipation that the respondent may not pay the rent in future. As per Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act, the notice of demand should be of arrears of rent and not of rent which may become arrears on a future date. To draw an analogy, reference can be made to RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 16 of 25 judgment titled Yogendra Pratap Singh Vs Savitri Pandey & Anr Criminal Appeal No. 1924 Of 2014 dated 19.09.2014 where the question was: Can cognizance of an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 be taken on the basis of a complaint filed before the expiry of the period of 15 days stipulated in the notice required to be served upon the drawer of the cheque in terms of Section 138 (c) of the Act aforementioned? This question was answered in the negative by full bench of the Apex Court, in the following words: "A complaint filed before expiry of 15 days from the date on which notice has been served on drawer/accused cannot be said to disclose the cause of action in terms of clause (c) of the proviso to Section 138 and upon such complaint which does not disclose the cause of action the Court is not competent to take cognizance. A conjoint reading of Section 138, which defines as to when and under what circumstances an offence can be said to have been committed, with Section 142(b) of the NI Act, that reiterates the position of the point of time when the cause of action has arisen, leaves no manner of doubt that no offence can be said to have been committed unless and until the period of 15 days, as prescribed under clause (c) of the proviso to Section 138, has, in fact, elapsed. Therefore, a Court is barred in law from taking cognizance of such complaint. It is not open to the Court to take cognizance of such a complaint merely because on the date of consideration or taking cognizance thereof a period of 15 days from the date on which the notice has been served on the drawer/accused has elapsed. We have no doubt that all the five essential features of Section 138 of the NI Act, as noted in the judgment of this Court in Kusum Ingots & Alloys Ltd. and which we have approved, must be satisfied for a complaint to be filed under Section 138. If the period prescribed in RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 17 of 25 clause (c) of the proviso to Section 138 has not expired, there is no commission of an offence nor accrual of cause of action for filing of complaint under Section 138 of the NI Act." Applying the same analogy, a legal notice issued before expiry of 15th of the subsequent month for rent of the preceding month cannot be said to disclose the cause of action in terms of clause (a) of sub section (1) to Section 14 of Delhi Rent Control Act, and upon such legal notice, the landlord is precluded from filing the eviction petition. If landlord prefers to file an eviction petition, the same is bound to fail due to his fault of issuing legal notice prior to the date on which the rent becomes due. A conjoint reading of Section 26 with Section 14(1)(a) of Delhi Rent Control Act, leaves no doubt that there is no cause of action to issue a legal notice demanding rent unless and until the rent is not paid till the due date, which in absence of a contract to the contrary, is the 15 th of succeeding month. It is not open to the Court to take into consideration such defective legal notice, merely because the said defective legal notice was posted after due date or the service was effected after due date. If on the date of issuance of legal notice, the respondent is not liable to pay any arrears of rent, then the said legal notice cannot form basis of an eviction petition. The petitioner was at liberty to issue a fresh legal notice for the same month after due date and thereby cure the defect in the legal notice issued RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 18 of 25 earlier prior to due date. The same has not been done. D. Because, Delhi Rent Control Act was enacted primarily with the basic objective of giving protection to the tenant, and to save them from harassment by avaricious and overbearing landlords. In the present case, the petitioner became the owner of the property on 20.04.2009 and for reasons best known to her, the petitioner approached her lawyer for issuing legal notice on or before 11.05.2009 and without waiting for the due date i.e. 15.05.2009, she issued legal notice to respondent on 11.05.2009. Immediately after acquiring interest in the property, the petitioner, in haste to fulfill her desire to procure possession of tenanted shop, issued demand notice for rent which was not even due on date of issuance of legal notice dated 11.05.2009. Against avaricious landlords, like the petitioner, the legislation has provided a safeguard to the tenants in the form of DRC Act and the provisions of the Act, being a Special Act , have to be construed strictly, keeping in mind the object behind its enactment. The issuance of legal notice and its non compliance has serious repercussions, thus, the legal notice has to be correctly issued by landlord for arrears of rent and in case the legal notice raises a valid demand, the tenant has a parallel obligation to strictly comply it within the time period RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 19 of 25 of 60 days by depositing the rent. Neither can the landlord claim any concession in issuing a defective notice, nor can the tenant seek any condonation in not depositing the rent within the time period of 60 days from date of receipt of notice. The tenant / respondent cannot be deprived of an opportunity to have the fullest benefit of statutory protection by liberal construction of a patently defective notice Ex.PW1/H demanding rent when it had not become due. E. Because, the legal notice Ex.PW1/H is not with respect to arrears of rent. The term "arrears due" cannot be extended to rent which has fallen due after issuance of notice of demand. In Daulat Ram vs Som Nath AIR 1981 Del 354 it has been held as under: "(11) The words 'the arrears of rent' in the expression "a notice of demand for the arrears of rent" used in this clause mean 'arrears of rent' legally recoverable which are to be paid or tendered by the tenant within two months of the service of a notice of demand. If rent was not legally recoverable on the date of notice of demand, the tenant would not be liable to pay or tender such amount. He is required to pay or tender what was legally recoverable and for which a demand has been made by the landlord by means of a notice. Unless there is demand for legally recoverable rent there is no liability of the tenant to pay or tender to defeat eviction proceedings. In the absence of demand of legally recoverable rent, cause of action for eviction does not accrue to a landlord. Further, there must be failure on the part of tenant to pay or tender the said legally recoverable rent within two months of the service of notice of demand. The expression "rent legally recoverable" means, 'rent' for RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 20 of 25 the recovery of which a suit can be filed. In other words, it means rent recovery of which is not barred by the law of limitation. The cause of action for eviction on the ground of non-payment of rent thus consists of the following facts : I)Relationship of landlord and tenant; ii) Existence of arrears of rent legally recoverable on the date of notice of demand; iii) Service of notice of demand in the manner provided in Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act; and iv) Failure of the tenant to pay or tender the whole of the arrears of rent legally recoverable from him within two months of the date of service of notice." (emphasis supplied) Though the said judgment deals with time barred arrears of rent, but the law (i.e. if rent was not legally recoverable on the date of notice of demand, the tenant would not be liable to pay or tender such amount) would be equally applicable to case of premature demand, as suit can also not be filed for recovery of rent which is not due. It would make no difference that the notice has been received by the tenant after due date, as to decide whether the legal notice demands arrears of rent or not, the date of notice and not the date of service is to be considered. Thus, the petitioner could not have demanded rent for the period of April 2009 by way of legal notice dated 11.05.2009 Ex.PW1/H. Till 11.05.2009, the cause of action for rent qua the month of April, 2009 was not ripe. 36. For the reasons recorded hereinabove, the demand notice dated 11.05.2009 Ex.PW1/H is defective and non est in the eyes of law. The present petition is without cause of action at the first instance. 37. The next question which arises for adjudication is RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 21 of 25 whether the demand notice Ex.PW1/H has been served upon the respondent. The respondent has disputed the service of demand notice Ex.PW1/H. The respondent/RW1, in her cross- examination, admitted that the address mentioned in the legal notice Ex.PW1/H is correct, however, she stated that the shop no. is not mentioned. It is not the case of the respondent that there is any other tenant by the same name as that of the respondent at the property in question. In the given scenario, it is to be presumed that the legal notice Ex.PW1/H was duly dispatched at the correct address of the respondent. Except for vague denial, the respondent has not produced any proof to substantiate the fact that legal notice Ex.PW1/H was not duly served upon her. The legal notice Ex.PW1/H having been sent by the petitioner via Postal Receipt Ex.PW1/I at correct address of the respondent is presumed to have been duly received by the respondent as per Section 27 of General Clauses Act and Section 114 (f) of Indian Evidence Act. The onus was upon the respondent to dislodge the said presumption by leading cogent evidence to the contrary. The respondent has failed to do so. Hence, it stands proved that the legal notice Ex.PW1/H was duly served upon the respondent. EXISTENCE OF ARREARS OF RENT AND ITS VALID TENDER 38. The petitioner has claimed the arrears of rent of the month of April, 2009 only. The respondent, per contra, averred RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 22 of 25 that she has been regularly making payment of rent to Smt. Amrita Tandon. A photocopy of rent receipt of the period 01.02.2009 to 31.07.2009 dt. 02.07.2009 is on record, however, the original rent receipt has neither been filed on record nor tendered in evidence. Be that as it may, the respondent had no obligation/duty to tender rent of the month of April, 2009 to the petitioner. 39. By virtue of registered GPA dated 28.09.07 Mark B, Ms. Amrita Tandon had the authority to collect rent on behalf of father of petitioner, Sh. Subhash Chand Tandon. As per Section 208 of Indian Contract Act, the termination of power of attorney holder, as regards third party, takes effect only from the time the third party obtains knowledge of it. 40. In the instant case, the petitioner has not sent any attornment letter to the respondent thereby informing her of execution of relinquishment deed in her favour. The petitioner has not filed any document/letter prior to demand notice dated 11.05.2009 Ex. PW1/H whereby she had informed the respondent that she has stepped into the shoes of erstwhile landlord Sh. Subhash Tandon and the agency/authority of Ms. Amrita Tandon has been terminated. The first communication to the respondent is the demand notice Ex. PW1/H which has been posted on 19.05.2009. The rent for the month of April 2009 had become due on 15.05.2009. The date of service of demand notice, i.e., 22.05.20093 will be construed as the date on which 3 The date of posting of demand notice is 19.05.2009 so the date of its service would be RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 23 of 25 the respondent received intimation regarding termination of authority of Ms. Amrita Tandon. The authority of Ms. Amrita Tandon to collect rent had terminated qua the respondent w.e.f. 22.05.2009. Ms. Amrita Tandon was well within her rights to receive the rent for the month of April 2009 which had become due on 15.05.2009. The petitioner, who had not informed the respondent about transfer of the tenanted shop in her favour, cannot claim rent for the month of April 2009 which Ms. Amrita Tandon was entitled to receive. Thus, the respondent was not bound to tender rent for the month of April, 2009 to the petitioner. 41. Before parting, it is pertinent to mention that respondent has alleged that present petition has not been instituted in correct name of tenant as her name is "Deepika Gupta" whereas eviction petition describes that as "Deepika". Mere mentioning of name of tenant without her surname is in no manner fatal as the identity of respondent/tenant is not disputed. CONCLUSION 42. In view of the foregoing reasons and discussion, the demand notice Ex.PW1/H, which is sine qua non for maintainability of the instant eviction petition, is held to be defective. The petitioner has also failed to prove the existence of arrears of rent as on date of issuance of demand notice. Moreover, the respondent was not under an obligation to tender 22.05.2009, i.e., after 3 days from the date of its posting by registered post. RC / ARC No. :108/2016 Rekha Satija vs. Deepika Page No. 24 of 25 the rent to the petitioner of the period demanded by way of legal notice. Consequently, the present eviction petition is dismissed.
